sections.en:
1 For he died in the year 785, more than ninety years old. Cf. below p. 231, n. 1.
2 Bar-Hebraeus, Histor. Dynast. ed. Pococke, Oxford, 1663, p. 148: "But this Theophilus was of the sect of the Maronites, who are a sect of Christians on Mount Lebanon."
3 Bar-Hebraeus, loc. cit.; cf. Wenrich, De auctorum Graecorum versionibus, 1842, p. 73 ff.
4 Rubens Duval, La littérature syriaque, p. 325; cf. Derenbourg, Mélanges Henri Weil, p. 118, n. 4.

6 Bar-Hebraeus, Hist. Dyn. ed. Pococke, p. 148: "He has an excellent history"; cf. Chronicon, ed. Bruns and Kirsch, p. 134: "He has an excellent book of histories in the Syriac language even if ... he blamed the orthodox," and p. 63 [Pococke]: "From the beginning of his empire (Seleucus Nicator) begins the era which is called of Alexander ... From Adam to the beginning of this epoch, according to the opinion of Theophilus of Rohes (= of Edessa), there are five thousand one hundred and ninety-seven years."

summary.headline: Theophilus of Edessa
summary.text: Introduction to Theophilus of Edessa, the eighth-century Christian Maronite scholar who transmitted Greek astrology to the Arabs. It discusses his education at Edessa, knowledge of Syriac and Greek, Syriac translations of Homer, disputed vowel notation, and a historical or chronological work praised by Bar-Hebraeus, before turning to Baghdad under Al-Mansur.
